text:
eli: Not sure if anyone else has had this but roofers were on the house this morning and somehow my internet started acting like its doing interpretive dance. huge jitter and packets dropping mid-call. pics of stomp-marked cable outside.
sophia: oh no. did they literally step on the coax/fiber? :grimacing: that can cause intermittent link drop even if physical damage isn't obvious. call the ISP and tell them "possible physical cable damage" so they prioritize.
tom: quick test: run ping with timestamps to capture the gaps. example: `ping -i 0.2 1.1.1.1 | ts` and attach the logfile to the ticket. helps the techs correlate to scheduled crew times.
eli: doing that now. here's a short sample (copied from terminal):
```
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=10 ttl=57 time=34.2 ms
Request timeout for icmp_seq 11
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=12 ttl=57 time=36.7 ms
Request timeout for icmp_seq 13
64 bytes from 1.1.1.1: icmp_seq=14 ttl=57 time=35.1 ms
--- 1.1.1.1 ping statistics ---
15 packets transmitted, 13 packets received, 13.3% packet loss
```
mike: that packet loss is enough to break zoom. if ISP dispatch is slow use phone hotspot as backup for critical meetings. tether + hotspot data saver in Zoom can keep you online.
eli: hotspot rescue worked for one meeting but battery died. ordered a small USB powerbank with passthrough so i can tether longer.
sophia: also tip: take a photo of the cable where the roofers were and note the time. ISP techs sometimes need proof to file an incident, and it speeds up repairs.
tom: if it's fiber and the outer jacket is crushed they may need an onsite splice. could take a few hours depending on crew. if copper/coax, they might be able to clamp/replace section quickly.
eli: ISP scheduled a truck roll for afternoon. thanks for tips. also, new policy: wearing hardhats doesn't exempt anyone from not touching other people's cables.
it-support-bot: heads-up: company loaner hotspots are available for same-day ship if you submit a request to #help with "loaner hotspot" in the subject. include urgent if it's for a meeting.
mike: pro tip: set Zoom to "Use original sound" and reduce video resolution while on tether to save bandwidth. also plug laptop into power when tethering to avoid battery draining too fast.
eli: getting a tiny travel router shipped to me tonight to create a better NAT/handoff from phone hotspot. might be useful for future chaos too.
sophia: gif: tiny roofer accidentally tangled in ethernet :joy:
tom: also: shoutout to local ISP field techs they deserve snacks. once they fixed my street two winters ago i mailed cookies.
eli: ISP tech arrived, found crushed jacket near the eave, swapped a short run and we're back to stable. thanks for all the tips and sympathy :relieved:
eli: attaching final speedtest just to close the loop: `Download 210 Mbps / Upload 18 Mbps / 12 ms ping`
it-support-bot: note: if you logged an internal incident for meetings disrupted by home connectivity, please update the ticket with final resolution so we can mark it closed.
